## Types

### type Cloner

```go
type Cloner interface { ... }
```

A Cloner is a hash function whose state can be cloned, returning a value with equivalent and independent state.

#### method Cloner.Clone

```go
Clone() (Cloner, error)
```

Clone returns an independent copy with equivalent state.

### type Hash

```go
type Hash interface { ... }
```

Hash is the common interface implemented by all hash functions.

Hash implementations in the standard library (e.g. [hash/crc32](hash/crc32.md) and [crypto/sha256](crypto/sha256.md)) implement the [encoding.BinaryMarshaler](encoding.md#type-binarymarshaler), [encoding.BinaryAppender](encoding.md#type-binaryappender), [encoding.BinaryUnmarshaler](encoding.md#type-binaryunmarshaler) and [Cloner](hash.md#type-cloner) interfaces. Marshaling a hash implementation allows its internal state to be saved and used for additional processing later, without having to re-write the data previously written to the hash. The hash state may contain portions of the input in its original form, which users are expected to handle for any possible security implications.

#### method Hash.Sum

```go
Sum([]byte) []byte
```

Sum appends the current hash to b and returns the resulting slice. It does not change the underlying hash state.

#### method Hash.Reset

```go
Reset()
```

Reset resets the Hash to its initial state.

#### method Hash.Size

```go
Size() int
```

Size returns the number of bytes Sum will return.

#### method Hash.BlockSize

```go
BlockSize() int
```

BlockSize returns the hash's underlying block size. The Write method must be able to accept any amount of data, but it may operate more efficiently if all writes are a multiple of the block size.

### type Hash32

```go
type Hash32 interface { ... }
```

Hash32 is the common interface implemented by all 32-bit hash functions.

#### method Hash32.Sum32

```go
Sum32() uint32
```

Sum32 returns the current 32-bit hash without changing the underlying state.
